page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is an instance within the High Frequency Compute lineup, configured with 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include a bundled 384 GB local NVMe SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent median performance for general system operations. Stress-ng delivers scores of 2411.16 on single-core and 8740.87 on multi-core testing, while Geekbench records 1625.0 for single-core and 4781.0 for multi-core. Clang software compilation benchmarks at 7042.0. However, uncached memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained, testing at 35.47 GB/sec for large block reads and 17.49 GB/sec for writes. Performance metrics also show lower throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 22.91 GB/sec and static web serving at 5.46 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU topology and lower uncached memory bandwidth, the server is ill-suited for intensive parallel machine learning tasks, as reflected in a low throughput of 4.89 tokens per second on 7B model generation. Instead, its resource allocation and rapid local NVMe storage deliver balanced capability for general-purpose application workloads, development staging environments, background task workers, and in-memory caches, evidenced by 6.0 million operations per second on Redis SET tests.
description: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 4 shared Intel x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz across 2 physical cores. It provides 16.0 GB of system memory and includes 384 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results place its compute capabilities within median ranges, including a Passmark CPU score of 7697.28 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4781.0. Cache handling shows solid throughput, reaching 6.0 million Redis SET operations per second, though uncached large-block memory bandwidth is limited to 35.47 GB/sec read and 17.49 GB/sec write. This instance configuration suits typical web backends, caching services, staging environments, and intermediate database layers needing fast local disk access rather than dedicated multi-threaded compute.
